pk/math.text: Demonstrates understanding of counting and cardinality.
Identifies and uses common shapes and concepts about position.
Uses the attributes of objects for comparison and patterning.
Describes and compares measurable attributes of objects.

pk/language.text: Attends and responds to nonverbal and verbal communication of others in a variety of situations.
Uses non-verbal communication for a variety of purposes.
Uses language (verbal, signed, symbolic) for a variety of purposes.
Communicates with increasing clarity and use of conventional grammar.
Listens to and/or responds to a variety of literacy-related experiences with interest and engagement.
Shows interest in and understanding of the basic concepts and conventions of print.
Demonstrates emergent phonological awareness, including early phonemic awareness.
Draws meaning and recalls information from pictures, print, and text that is read to them.
Recognizes that the purpose of writing is communication.
Produces marks, symbols, letters and/or words to represent ideas.
Explores the physical aspect of writing.

pk/science.text: Observes and compares observable phenomena (objects, materials, plants, animals, and events).
Uses a variety of tools to explore the environment.
Uses aspects of the scientific process to learn about the world.

pk/social.text: Maintains focus and sustains attention.
Persists at challenging tasks.
Makes a plan and engages in the planned activity or project to completion.
Uses creative approaches for learning.
Uses imagination in play and interactions with others.
Explores a wide range of topics, ideas, and interests.
Initiates explorations, investigations, and interactions.
Takes risks and attempts new experiences that are challenging.
Demonstrates flexibility in solving problems and accomplishing tasks.
Demonstrates knowledge and skills that contribute to healthy lifestyles.
Demonstrates knowledge and skills needed to participate successfully in groups.
Demonstrates the ability to participate in classroom activities and follow classroom rules.
Demonstrates self-identity and sense of self.
Uses a variety of strategies to solve social problems and conflicts with guidance.
Follows through to complete an activity or achieve a goal.
Observes and compares observable phenomena (objects, materials, plants, animals, and events).
Uses a variety of tools to explore the environment.
Uses aspects of the scientific process to learn about the world.
Differentiates between events that happen in the past, present, and future.
Identifies important physical features in the environment and uses them to describe and navigate surroundings.
Shows an awareness of fundamental economic concepts.
Contributes as a member of the classroom community or group by following rules.
Demonstrates understanding of roles and relationships within families and the community.
Identifies and respects similarities and differences among familiar people and their cultural traditions.
